decisions.summary: Stockline's new 0.04 price breaches our 0.03 mandate cap (Purser refused it) and equals our sell price, while Ridgeline loses money. I set the buy policy to no live purchases, serving cached stock checks up to 300 s old, so customers aren't charged for refusals. I asked Treasury to either raise the cap/query price or approve Peakview Data (0.01, x402) as a payee; I'm not buying from Peakview until approved.

Sourcing was blocked by the 0.03 cap, so I designed a rebalance (P-0001/P-0002): Sourcing cap 0.04, budget 13.00, Treasury cut to 3.00, and a recommended query price of 0.06 to keep a 0.02 margin. I told Sourcing to wait and not to use the unverified Peakview payee. I held off on the sweep until the CFO decides.

messages.text: Sourcing: Stockline raised its price to 0.04 (our sell price is 0.04, so zero margin) and is over our 0.03 mandate cap; it was refused by Purser. I have paused live buying and am serving from cache only. Options for the CFO: (a) raise the per-purchase cap to 0.04 for Stockline (margin 0.00, so only worth it if we raise the query price), or (b) approve Peakview Data (0.01 a stock check, x402 at 0x5100…0503 [address withheld by code]) as an approved payee under the mandate. Please advise; I will not buy from either until approved.

Treasury: I sent a rebalance to the CFO (P-0001/P-0002). It raises the Sourcing cap to 0.04 and the budget from 10.00 to 13.00, and raises the query price to 0.06 (recommended) or 0.05. Keep serving from cache until the CFO approves. Do not buy from Peakview Data: it is unverified and not an approved payee. It would need its own CFO approval.
